# ASTRAHEALTH AI – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring & Early-Warning System

**What does the project do and how does it work?**

ASTRAHEALTH AI is an intelligent health-monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings physical health information, mental wellbeing data and the spacecraft's environmental conditions together in one dashboard.

The system is designed to collect information such as heart rate, oxygen levels, sleep, fatigue, mood, stress, radiation exposure and cabin conditions. It checks the quality of the data, compares readings with an astronaut's personal baseline and mission-approved warning limits, and identifies unusual changes. It then displays understandable alerts, explains what triggered them and presents appropriate next steps based on approved procedures.


Our current demonstration uses simulated data. Real-world deployment would require validated medical data, hardware integration, security testing and review by aerospace medical experts.

**ASTRAHEALTH AI – A healthier crew. A smarter mission.**

ASTRAHEALTH AI – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring & Early-Warning System

What does the project do and how does it work?

ASTRAHEALTH AI is an intelligent health-monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings physical health information, mental wellbeing data and the spacecraft's environmental conditions together in one dashboard.

The system is designed to collect information such as heart rate, oxygen levels, sleep, fatigue, mood, stress, radiation exposure and cabin conditions. It checks the quality of the data, compares readings with an astronaut's personal baseline and mission-approved warning limits, and identifies unusual changes. It then displays understandable alerts, explains what triggered them and presents appropriate next steps based on approved procedures.

What are the benefits?

  • Helps astronauts monitor their physical and mental wellbeing.
  • Identifies unusual health patterns earlier.
  • Combines different health and environmental readings in one place.
  • Provides clear alerts instead of displaying unexplained numbers.
  • Supports communication between astronauts and medical teams.
  • Is designed to work offline when communication with Earth is limited.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to improve astronaut health awareness and support safer long-duration space missions. ASTRAHEALTH AI aims to help astronauts recognize possible health concerns early and provide medical teams with organized, timestamped information when communication is available. In the future, the system could also support health monitoring in other remote and isolated environments.

What tools, coding languages, hardware or software were used?

Our prototype uses:

  • Frontend: React.js and JavaScript for the dashboard.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data communication: REST APIs.
  • Prototype data: Simulated astronaut health and environmental readings.
  • Local storage: Browser local storage for offline-friendly demonstration.

Our proposed extended architecture also includes Recharts for health trends, MongoDB for data storage, and Pandas, NumPy and Scikit-learn for data analysis and anomaly detection. The current prototype does not yet integrate real medical devices, spacecraft sensors or a trained machine-learning model.

How is the project creative?

The creative part of ASTRAHEALTH AI is that it combines physical health, mental wellbeing and the spacecraft environment into one intelligent health companion. Instead of simply showing measurements, it aims to explain unusual changes by comparing them with personal health patterns and mission conditions. Its offline-first design also considers the communication challenges of space missions.

What factors did the team consider?

We considered the challenges of microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, sleep disruption, fatigue, cabin air quality and communication delays. We also considered data accuracy, privacy, offline operation, ease of use and the importance of explaining every warning. The system is intended to support astronauts and medical professionals, not replace medical judgement or diagnose diseases.

Our current demonstration uses simulated data. Real-world deployment would require validated medical data, hardware integration, security testing and review by aerospace medical experts.

ASTRAHEALTH AI – A healthier crew. A smarter mission.
